newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - March 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - March 13.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Thursday's Daily Variety:

* HOLLYWOOD - A November trial date has been set for former Disney studio chairman Jeffrey Katzenberg's $250 million breach-of-contract suit against the company. On Wednesday, Los Angeles Superior Court Judge John Ouderkirk scheduled a status conference for November 13 and a trial date of November 18. Katzenberg, who left Disney in 1994 after being passed over for a promotion, is seeking $250 million from his former employer.

* NEW YORK - After a nearly year-long courtship, Westinghouse's CBS has won Bryant Gumbel for a $5 million-a-year payday that also includes stock options in the company. Gumbel, who left the "Today" show on General Electric's NBC in January after 15 years, is by far the most prominent black journalist on TV, and his hiring marks a major coup for CBS News, long a distant third in the news race.

* NEW YORK - Interscope, whose biggest hit was the Robin Williams movie "Jumanji," based on Chris Van Allsburg's children's book, has signed the author to a three-picture deal. The first film under the new pact will be adapted from another Van Allsburg fantasy book, "The Widow's Broom." Van Allsburg will form a production company with partner Bill Teitler, who helped produce "Jumanji". Van Allsburg and Teitler will adapt the fantasy books and have a discretionary fund to acquire outside projects to produce.

* NEW YORK - Motion Picture Association of America president Jack Valenti staunchly defended the current TV program ratings system Wednesday -- despite congressional protest over the current age-based warnings and despite his earlier acknowledgement that the industry may accept some changes. At a panel session, Valenti said he'd resist attempts by Sen. Joseph Lieberman and others to extend the program ratings to warn about specific violence, sex or language content in TV series.

* HOLLYWOOD - "The English Patient" has added to its growing list of accolades in the buildup to the Oscars, taking top honors Wednesday night at the Producers Guild of America Awards. Producer Saul Zaentz received the group's Darryl F. Zanuck award as producer of the year and the guild's Eastman Kodak Vision Award. The picture also won top honors for director Anthony Minghella on Saturday at the Directors Guild of America Awards, and several weeks ago John Seale won for its cinematography.
